chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, who said:

The Imam, the Knowledgeable One, عليه السلام, was asked, "How is the knowledge of Allah?" He said, "He knew, and willed, and intended, and measured, and decreed, and executed. So He executed what He decreed, and decreed what He measured, and measured what He intended. Thus by His knowledge was the will, and by His will was the intention, and by His intention was the measuring, and by His measuring was the decree, and by His decree was the execution."
And knowledge is prior to will, and will is second, and intention is third, and measuring falls upon decree through execution.

So for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, there is al-badāʾ regarding what He knows, whenever He wills, and regarding what He intends for the measuring of things. But when the decree takes place through execution, then there is no badāʾ. Thus knowledge concerning the known is before its coming to be, and will concerning what is brought forth is before its concrete existence, and intention concerning the intended is before its establishment, and the measuring of these known things is before their detailing and their arrival into observable existence and time.

And decree through execution is that which is made firm among the effected things possessing bodies, perceived by the senses, among those having color, smell, weight, and measure, and whatever creeps and moves among humans, jinn, birds, beasts, and other than that which is perceived by the senses.

So for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in that there is badāʾ regarding what has no concrete entity. But when the concrete, understood, perceived thing takes place, then there is no badāʾ. And Allah does whatever He wills.

So by knowledge He knew things before their being; by will He made known their attributes and their limits and brought them forth before manifesting them; by intention He distinguished their essences in their colors and attributes; by measuring He measured their sustenances and made known their beginning and their end; by decree He clarified their places to people and guided them to them; and by execution He explained their causes and made their affair clear.
And that is the measuring of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.

key_terms.التَّقْدِيرُ: Divine measuring or apportioning before detailed manifestation.
key_terms.الْإِرَادَةُ: Divine intention that distinguishes the intended entities in their qualities.
key_terms.الْإِمْضَاءُ: Divine execution or final carrying out of what has been decreed.
key_terms.الْبَدَاءُ: Manifestation of a change in the divine course before final execution.
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: Divine knowledge that precedes all stages of bringing things into being.
key_terms.الْقَضَاءُ: Divine decree by which matters are fixed and clarified.
key_terms.الْمَشِيئَةُ: Divine will through which the attributes and boundaries of things are specified.
key_terms.الْمَعْلُومِ: That which is known by Allah before its coming into existence.

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Allah’s knowledge, will, decree, and al-badāʾ?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ordered relationship between divine knowledge, will, intention, measuring, decree, and execution in the unfolding of creation. It also discusses al-badāʾ within the domain before final execution, while affirming that once decree is executed in concrete existence, there is no badāʾ. The text presents a theological account of divine knowledge and decree in a structured and hierarchical form.
